comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT. Extrude and Replace Face on a reported design (GitHub mitcad/Mitcad#674, mitcad#2538; opened with --open, never committed; tools/cli/extrude-replace-reported-test.cmake): a dome of R 70 revolved about z (Revolve1, its flat top a disk of R 63.25 at 30 mm, its open side a disk of R 70 at 0), the top's edge rounded R 16 (Fillet1, a rounding between a plane and a sphere), shelled 2 mm inside with the R 70 side open (Shell1: a bowl, its rim the ring from R 68 to R 70). Extrude1 joins a cross of ribs inside it, from Plane1 (8 mm inside the top, at 22 mm) up to the inside of the top (at 28 mm), To Selected Face; the ribs' ends reach R 70 as seen along z, past the bowl's outside at that height (R 66.0), and ReplaceFace1 puts those four ends onto the outer rounding. Sketch3 lies on the rim: a tab under one rib, from an arc of R 58 out to a straight end whose corners lie on the R 70 circle (the end itself at R 68.6 in its middle).

Before mitcad#2538 the four new ends lay on a copy of the rounding's surface (a B-spline continued past its edges) and the rounding itself on the original, so the merge after the cut left them apart: four outlines on the smooth rounding (the report's second picture). Now the rounding moves onto the continued surface too and the ends merge with it: one face holds the rounding's name and the new faces' name, and no face is a replaced end alone.

Extrude1 up to the first face of the body ahead, To Next or up to the body: the parts of the ribs past the bowl's outside at 22 mm (R 66.0 to the R 70 ends) meet no face above, as the bowl's outside lies below 22 mm there. Both fail in words; only To Selected Face (a plane at 28 mm) ends them, past the bowl, which ReplaceFace1 then trims.

does not cut across the whole profile: a part of the profile passes beside the target

comment: Back as saved. The saved Extrude1 names the hub's middle region (inside the hub circle c2, between the inner ends of three ribs) as it was before the fourth rib (c33 to c36) was drawn: that rib's inner end (c34) crosses the hub circle and now splits the region into the middle and a segment between c34 and the circle, so the reference is found as those two regions and Extrude1 builds from both with the warning that says so (mitcad#407), as it does when the design is opened.

expect.error_contains: c34[c2+c33,c2+c35]} after a change in Sketch2

comment: Sketch3 lies on the rim, the ring from R 68 to R 70; its R 70 circle (c1) is the outline the sketch got when it was made, and the rim's inner edge at R 68 is the face's own. The tab is an area of the sketch's own curves, so it is one profile keyed by them alone (mitcad#2197), whatever the rim's edges cross it; the steps below use that key. The rest of Sketch3's profiles (the sliver past the tab's end, the rim around it) are the sketch's matter, not checked here.

The report's third picture: the tab joined into the bowl (Flip) up to the rib's underside To Adjacent Faces (the face, here the cross's underside, and the faces next to it: the ribs' sides, the hub's side and the inner rounding where the ribs meet the wall). Over the tab's inner part they end it: under the rib at its underside (22 mm), from R 63.64 to R 65.67 at the inner rounding. From R 65.67 (where the inner rounding meets the inner spherical wall) out to the tab's end the first face above is the inner spherical wall, tangent to the rounding but not next to the underside, so no face of the target; the tab's end also lies on the rim itself (from R 68), inside the wall from the start. That part has no end: the error says it meets the body only at faces that are not the target and points to the body as the object.

expect.error_contains: does not cut across the whole profile: a part of the profile meets the target's body only at faces

comment: Up to the body each part of the tab ends at the body's first face above it: under the rib at its underside, then at the inner rounding and the inner wall, and the part on the rim where it leaves the wall. The Join builds. (Before, OCCT's face merge after the Join failed on its result with 'V parameters out of range' and so did the Join; the result now keeps its faces as the operation left them, mitcad#2538.)
